title: ZCC entitlement calls: response and update body shapes

prose.text: Paths and methods are in the generated API surface. The shapes are where the sources part ways. What the settings mean is in [[zcc.entitlements]].

prose.label: Reading.
prose.text: The API document and a recorded response return one object per call, while the Go SDK reads a list {{divergence:get-response-shape}}. The Python SDK accepts either: [[zcc.sdk-python.entitlements:single-object-wrapped]].

prose.label: Writing.
prose.text: The update body in the API document is not the shape the Go SDK sends {{divergence:update-body-shape}}. The Python SDK sends an empty body: [[zcc.sdk-python.entitlements:python-update-empty-body]]. What the API does with an empty update is open {{gap:empty-update-effect}}.

checks.do: Before scripting a change, compare the body your client sends with the API document's update body.
Before relying on a Go SDK read, check whether the tenant returns one object or a list.

get-response-shape.summary: Whether a GET of ZPA or ZDX entitlements returns one object or a list

positions.says: The API document's response is a single object holding `groupList`, `deviceGroupList`, the switches and `totalCount` (the ZDX response likewise), with `page`, `pageSize` and `search` parameters.
The Go SDK decodes each page into a list of entitlement objects and pages until a page is shorter than the page size.
Recorded responses from one test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) are a single JSON object for both the ZPA and the ZDX call, with and without paging parameters.

get-response-shape.impact: The API document and the one recorded tenant agree on a single object. The Go SDK decodes the body into a list, which does not fit that shape, so a Go read of entitlements is likely to fail on such a tenant; whether any tenant returns a list is not shown. The Python SDK's single-object wrapping was removed as a position (verifier w2 E1): it accepts either shape and takes no side.

update-body-shape.summary: What the update body for ZPA or ZDX entitlements contains

positions.says: The API document's update body uses `enableForAll`, `computeDeviceGroups`, `groupIds`, `groupNames`, `deviceGroupIds`, `deviceGroupNames` and `machineTunEnabledForAll` (ZDX: `logoutZCC` instead of the machine tunnel field), and returns a success envelope.

quotes: resp, err := service.Client.NewZccRequestDo(ctx, "PUT", updateZpaGroupEndpoint, nil, bytes.NewBuffer(body), nil)

positions.says: The Go SDK sends the read shape back: `zpaEnableForAll`, `groupList` and `deviceGroupList` objects, `computeDeviceGroupsForZPA`, and decodes the response as an entitlement object.

update-body-shape.impact: A Go SDK update may send keys the endpoint does not read, so an entitlement change can appear to succeed without taking effect.

empty-update-effect.title: What the update endpoints do with an empty body
empty-update-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Whether the API silently no-ops or errors on empty PUTs is unverified." In one recorded test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette), the Python SDK's empty-body PUTs to both update paths returned HTTP 404 Not Found, while GETs on the same tenant succeeded; whether the 404 comes from the empty body or from the path at that gateway is not shown.
